answer: Spare-key shops still flood the roll with twins cut from one jig. A recruit hangs a 2.4-meter timber sounding-post in a public hall for 11 days, bonded with 44 POA. Each dawn a warden strikes it and posts a frequency mirror of 17 taps whose overtone ranks sit 6-11 cents apart; the post's umber resin stain, scanned at 400 dpi, may not collide with another key. Auditors replay the hall mic log against the stain hash. Cost: 44 POA locked 11 days. If two keys share a post, a stain map matches within 2.2%, or a mirror series is reused, 52% of the bond burns and that lot is barred for 5 epochs.
